intro: Wrestling is one of the oldest sports in the world: two athletes try to take each other down, expose the opponent's back to the mat and ultimately pin both shoulders for a fall. Olympic wrestling has two styles — freestyle, where legs can be attacked, and Greco-Roman, where all holds must be above the waist. United World Wrestling (UWW) publishes the international rules.
inThirtySeconds: Pin both of your opponent's shoulders to the mat for a fall — instant victory.
Score points with takedowns, exposures and pushing your opponent out.
A big enough points lead ends the bout early (technical superiority).
Greco-Roman: no attacking the legs and no using your legs to trip.
objective: Win by fall, by technical superiority, or by points after two 3-minute periods.

scoring.label: Takedown
scoring.detail: Taking the opponent down to the mat under control; more for high-amplitude throws.

scoring.label: Exposure
scoring.detail: Turning the opponent's back towards the mat (danger position).

scoring.label: Step out
scoring.detail: The opponent steps out of the protection area.

scoring.label: Fall
scoring.detail: Both shoulders held to the mat.

variants.name: Freestyle
variants.description: Holds anywhere on the body, including leg attacks.

variants.name: Greco-Roman
variants.description: Holds only above the waist; legs can't be used to attack or trip.

rules.title: The fall (pin)
rules.summary: Holding both of the opponent's shoulders on the mat long enough for the referee to confirm control ends the bout.
rules.body: A fall wins regardless of the score. The referee slaps the mat to confirm it.

rules.title: Technical superiority
rules.summary: A large enough points lead stops the bout early: 10 points in freestyle and 8 in Greco-Roman.
rules.body: If neither wrestler reaches a fall or technical superiority, the winner is the one with more points. Ties are broken by the highest-value hold, fewest cautions, and the last point scored.

rules.title: Takedowns and exposure
rules.summary: A takedown scores 2 points or more; turning an opponent's back towards the mat scores 2 (the 'gut wrench' is a classic way).
rules.body: Big throws that carry the opponent through the air directly into danger position can score 4 or 5 points.

rules.title: Passivity
rules.summary: A wrestler who avoids wrestling can be called passive, giving the opponent a chance to score.
rules.body: In freestyle, the passive wrestler gets a 30-second activity period; if they don't score, the opponent gets a point. In Greco-Roman, passivity can give the opponent a point and the choice to restart in the par terre (ground) position.

chapters.title: The two styles
chapters.summary: What changes between freestyle and Greco-Roman.

rules.title: Greco-Roman: above the waist
rules.summary: It is forbidden to grab the opponent's legs or use your own legs to trip, lift or apply holds.
rules.body: This makes Greco-Roman a game of upper-body clinches, arm drags and dramatic lifts and throws.

rules.title: Freestyle: legs are fair game
rules.summary: Wrestlers may attack the legs with shots, single-leg and double-leg takedowns.
rules.body: Freestyle is the style practised by women in the Olympics, and by men alongside Greco-Roman.

fouls.name: Fleeing the hold or mat
fouls.description: Avoiding contact or stepping out to escape.
fouls.consequence: Caution and points to the opponent

fouls.name: Illegal hold
fouls.description: Dangerous holds such as neck cranks or twisting joints.

fouls.name: Leg foul (Greco)
fouls.description: Using or attacking the legs in Greco-Roman.
fouls.consequence: Caution and points to the opponent

flow.title: First period
flow.description: Three minutes from the standing position.

flow.title: Second period
flow.description: Three minutes; the referee raises the winner's hand.

field.name: Mat
field.dimensions: 9 m diameter wrestling area, plus a protection zone
notes: Red passivity zone near the edge

glossary.definition: Bringing the opponent to the mat from standing.
Turning an opponent over from the ground.
Restart with one wrestler on hands and knees.

funFacts: Wrestling was introduced to the ancient Olympic Games in 708 BC.
Women's freestyle wrestling joined the Olympic programme in 2004.
